id_and_class.summary: Skopelitou argues that language, which she calls Logos, is the precondition of consciousness: consciousness becomes possible, and the world becomes meaningful, only through language. Because every question about consciousness, every concept, and every scientific instrument is framed in words, she presents Logos as a meta-theory that dissolves the materialism versus idealism debate.

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is constituted through language. If everything, including time, space, selfhood, and the universe, is first of all a word, then consciousness and all it entails is a word too.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Skopelitou declines to take a side: she treats both materialism and idealism as narrative frameworks built in and through language, so the mind-body question is reframed as a question about linguistic framing.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not applicable (language is the ground that makes consciousness possible, so consciousness neither emerges from matter nor stands as a primitive of its own)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Subjectivity comes from reflexivity, making oneself the subject of one's own sentences. Skopelitou says this recursive loop gives consciousness its feel of inner awareness, self-awareness, and aboutness.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Qualia, like subjectivity and self-awareness, already presuppose symbolic mediation; they are knowable and sayable only as framed in Logos.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Logos (language as the foundational structure of meaning); all other entities, including neural signals and the external world, are treated as linguistic constructs.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Through reflection on the conditions of asking about consciousness, starting from Cartesian doubt. Skopelitou holds that empirical inputs are always inferred and described in agreed terms, so they never give language-free access.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Words and symbolic structures, organized recursively so that a speaker can take herself as the subject of her own sentences.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Self-awareness, Intentionality (aboutness), Meaning; Phenomenal (as linguistically framed)
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Logos reverses the usual question: instead of asking what consciousness is, it asks what must be in place for that question to arise, and answers that it is language.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Skopelitou rejects the brain-as-host model as untestable, so consciousness is located in linguistic and symbolic structures rather than in a brain region.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Language lets a person reflect and draw distinctions, which is what makes consciousness matter to anyone. Without Logos there would be no ‘us’ for whom consciousness could matter.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: All input, including neural signals, reaches us as named patterns detected by instruments we built and described in terms we agreed on. Perception of others and of the outside world already happens within prior linguistic frameworks.
core_claims_and_evidence: Even doubting one's own consciousness relies on words such as ‘I’, ‘am’, and ‘consciousness’, so language is prior to any formulation of consciousness.
Materialism and idealism are both narratives constructed in language, so Logos stands beneath them as a meta-theory.
Claims about animal or AI consciousness depend on how coherent our linguistic projections are, so non-human consciousness cannot be posed or verified outside language.
Any attempt to refute Logos must use language, which Skopelitou takes as making the theory testable yet non-falsifiable.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Skopelitou herself calls the view non-falsifiable, and the self-confirming argument (any refutation uses language) risks making the thesis immune to evidence. Her strong claim that consciousness arises through language sits awkwardly with her willingness to allow that animals or AI may have some form of experience.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: If all thought is mediated by words, it remains unclear whether consciousness without language could ever be known. The view does not say what language itself is grounded in or how it first arose.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Coherent as a meta-theory about the framing of consciousness research, but it blurs the line between the claim that consciousness is known through language and the claim that it exists only through language.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Skopelitou does not rule out some form of AI experience, but holds that any judgment about it is a linguistic projection we cannot verify independently.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Meaning, on this view, is made by language and by the reflexive speakers who use it, with no further cosmic purpose proposed.
